complexity: High: asynchronous lock ownership must remain coupled to every audio.play() and release only after audio stops; transfer, cancellation, timeout, stale events, media errors, and teardown interact.
Moderate-high: shared controller behavior must be wired into both fixed and discovery resources and checked in the actual delivered HTML/CSP.
evidence: factory/work-items/DIAL-003/PRODUCT.md and TECH.md specify same-profile/device ownership, takeover, shared Pause, fail-closed bounded behavior, Web Locks plus BroadcastChannel, no server coordination, and actual-host verification.

factory/work-items/DIAL-003/state.json records human approval of exact PRODUCT.md and TECH.md hashes (3dc151e49b28a8c555482db1cbe888b69c9b91b30e7044223ac8bf3a9970f19e and 686e2f79f643581f8aa3aa0c88c05202d15baf88e8f97d94ce4ab7f3f74f12db). DIAL-004 reuses that approved architecture and behavior; no new server fallback or broader scope is requested.

factory/work-items/DIAL-003/evidence/owner-probe-results.md reports paired frames with BroadcastChannel nonce round trips, Web Lock contention, transfer pause/release/ack before new acquisition and play in both directions, and one explicit heard=true/playback=true observation.
The same DIAL-003 evidence explicitly says lock-holder close/remount recovery was not recorded; it also cautions that the probe is feasibility evidence, not implementation of regular player behavior.
src/player-controller.ts currently has no BroadcastChannel/Web Locks integration and starts audio directly; the requested product implementation remains to be built.
relevant_code: src/player-controller.ts: installPlayer currently owns local attempt/state handling and calls audio.play() directly; this is the main integration point.
src/player.ts: installs the controller for the fixed resource and, when discovery elements exist, the country player; the shared controller path can cover both.
public/player.html and public/discovery.html: delivered UI resources embed the controller script and need the shared remote status/Pause affordance.
src/server.ts: builds and registers fixed/discovery HTML resources; resource versioning and delivered-resource checks are relevant to packaging.
test/player.test.js and test/ui-harness.js: existing local playback and delivered-resource test surfaces; no cross-frame coordinator or shared-lock tests were found.
risks: A messaging acknowledgment alone is not proof of lock exclusion; only the lock holder may start audio, with no speculative start on timeout or unavailable APIs.
Simultaneous requests, canceled Play, stale/delayed acknowledgments, and unresponsive or backgrounded owners can cause overlap or stale state if ownership and attempt IDs are not enforced.
The probe's close/remount case remains unverified and must be retained as a mandatory feature verification criterion, not represented as already working.
Host storage partition, frame lifecycle, and post-transfer user activation may differ outside the tested browser/profile/device; do not claim broader support or add a server fallback.
scope: Integrate the approved same-profile/device Web Locks and BroadcastChannel takeover/shared Pause behavior into both regular Dial players, fail closed, and retain unverified close/remount recovery as mandatory verification; no server fallback.
spec_decision: Skip a new Spec: DIAL-003 PRODUCT.md/TECH.md are already approved at exact revisions, and DIAL-004 asks to implement the same approved behavior in regular players. DIAL-004 should be recorded as an explicitly justified spec skip. Preserve DIAL-003's unverified close/remount recovery as required implementation verification; do not claim the probe demonstrated it.
